corrections.topic: Replace the proposal JUNO with SuperJ6
corrections.finding: Both bass parts expose the two wave layers, their separate PWM flags and widths, Sub level, and three LFO mode/rate pairs. The 944 tempo field showed a normalized coordinate. Literal original tempo labels remain open.

corrections.topic: Remove Chicago’s duplicate raw field list
corrections.finding: Chicago’s 20 scalar fields are indexed individually. The duplicate list on the right was removed.

corrections.topic: Show a discrete wave or blend; morph the glyph
corrections.finding: Chicago shows SAW. The MIAMI carrier shows SQR and XMod SAW. Printed wave names are established. The original 17:00 artwork and value-dependent shape behavior across these fields remain unverified. Separately, all 83 editable drum fields had fixed endpoint SVG paths at 944.

corrections.topic: Gesture-only roll without tool modes or a separate inspector; single switchable lane
corrections.finding: The mounted note buttons and lane controls are indexed. Eight desktop modes were visited. This walk supplies no gesture-by-gesture test.

corrections.topic: Add a musical playhead and hierarchy for bar/beat divisions
corrections.finding: Beat labels and the trace-start marker were captured. A moving selected-part playhead and exact bar/beat contrast remain unverified.

corrections.topic: Use desktop components and type scale on portrait phones
corrections.finding: The same named roll, lane and level controls render at 390×844. Matching components is observed; all font/weight/spacing values and design acceptance are not established.

corrections.topic: Retain the owner’s 17:00 glyphs and standardize on the R22 radius/type scale
corrections.finding: The drawings identify candidate glyphs. The 944 captures preserve visual output. No approved 17:00 asset-key manifest or pixel-matched cross-surface collection establishes full retention.

corrections.topic: Port the visual system to product site and firmware together
corrections.finding: The receipts here cover the web Remote. The separate 240×240 Chicago firmware frame shows 125 BPM and Cutoff 100%, while the PDF/browser show 120 BPM and 25%. Joint visual acceptance remains open.
